question: Is default-enabled operator.write access to local Claude transcript history across the Gateway and paired nodes the intended security and upgrade boundary?
rationale: Code review can validate containment and authorization mechanics, but maintainers must explicitly accept exposing sensitive local history by default and requiring paired-node command upgrades.

options.title: Accept default read-only access
options.body: Keep default activation after the discovery and lifecycle defects are fixed and fresh-install plus upgrade proof is complete.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve lazy activation and expose the Claude session catalog only after the user enables it.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Hold the PR until a narrower transcript-access and activation model is selected.

recommendation.title: Accept default read-only access
recommendation.body: Keep default activation after the discovery and lifecycle defects are fixed and fresh-install plus upgrade proof is complete.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the adjacent session-fleet implementation and has the strongest available product and repository ownership signal.
